title: TDS Returns in Forms 138 and 140: Q3 2026-27 Due by 31 January 2027
excerpt: Forms 24Q and 26Q are now Forms 138 and 140. Learn the new TDS forms and sections, the October–December 2026 deposit and filing dates, and the fees for late filing.
body:
From 1 April 2026, TDS in India runs under the Income-tax Act, 2025 and the Income-tax Rules, 2026. The familiar Forms 24Q and 26Q have been replaced, section numbers have changed, and the software you use to prepare returns has new codes. If you deduct TDS on salaries, rent, professional fees or contractor payments, the October–December 2026 quarter is a good time to check that your process has caught up.

This article explains the new forms, the dates coming up for this quarter, and the costs of getting it wrong.

## What has changed

The basic idea of TDS is the same. You deduct tax when you pay certain amounts, deposit it with the government, file a quarterly statement and give the payee a certificate. What has changed is the names and numbers.

- **Salary TDS** now falls under **section 392** of the new Act (earlier section 192).
- **TDS on other payments** to residents and non-residents, such as rent, professional fees, contractor payments and commission, is now brought together under **section 393** (earlier spread across sections 194C, 194H, 194I, 194J and others).
- The quarterly statement for salary TDS is now **Form 138** (earlier Form 24Q).
- The quarterly statement for non-salary TDS is now **Form 140** (earlier Form 26Q).
- The TCS quarterly statement is now **Form 143** (earlier Form 27EQ).
- The salary TDS certificate is now **Form 130** (earlier Form 16), and the non-salary certificate is **Form 131** (earlier Form 16A).

The return utilities and nature-of-payment codes have also been updated. Old section references like "194J" will not work in the new forms. Each payment must be reported under its new code.

## Key dates for the October–December 2026 quarter

- **7 December 2026:** deposit TDS deducted in November 2026.
- **7 January 2027:** deposit TDS deducted in December 2026.
- **31 January 2027:** file Form 138 and Form 140 for the October–December 2026 quarter.

TDS deducted in any month is generally due by the 7th of the next month. March is the exception, with a later date for tax deducted that month. For the January–March 2027 quarter, the salary and non-salary statements are due by 31 May 2027.

Employers will issue Form 130 to employees for the first time for tax year 2026-27. It is due by 15 June 2027 and must be generated from the TRACES portal. Form 16 continues for salary paid in FY 2025-26.

## Things to check before you file

Many deductors filed their first two quarters on the new forms with some confusion. Before the Q3 statement, review these points.

- **Correct form for each payment.** Salary goes in Form 138. Rent, fees, contract and other resident payments go in Form 140. Do not mix them.
- **New section codes.** Map every vendor payment to the new code in your accounting or TDS software. A wrong code can cause a mismatch in the payee's tax credit.
- **Challan split.** If one challan covers both salary and non-salary TDS, the amount has to be allocated correctly across the forms before filing.
- **PAN of every payee.** A missing or invalid PAN usually means tax at a higher rate and errors in the statement.
- **Lower deduction certificates.** If a vendor has a lower or nil deduction certificate, check that it is valid for the period and quoted correctly.
- **Updated software.** Use the latest return preparation utility and validation tool. Returns built on old utilities may be rejected.

## What happens if you are late

The penalties are broadly the same as before, under new section numbers.

- **Late filing fee:** ₹200 for every day the statement is late, under section 427 of the new Act (earlier section 234E). The total fee cannot exceed the TDS amount, and it must be paid before the statement is filed.
- **Late deduction:** interest at **1% per month** from the date tax should have been deducted.
- **Late deposit:** interest at **1.5% per month** from the date of deduction until it is paid.
- **Penalty:** a separate penalty can apply for not filing a statement or filing incorrect details.
- **Expense disallowance:** if TDS is not deducted or paid, part of the expense may not be allowed when computing your business income.

Late or wrong filing also hurts the people you pay. Their credit will not show in their tax records, which leads to follow-up calls and strained relationships with employees and vendors.

## A simple routine that works

Small businesses usually manage TDS well with a monthly habit. Record TDS when you book each bill. Pay the challan before the 7th. Reconcile the challans with your books at the end of each quarter, then file within the first two weeks of the following month instead of waiting for the last day.
